claims.text: Spin-polarized DFT+DMFT with an adjustable Coulomb U can accurately capture ferromagnetic ground states.
DFT+DMFT explains ferromagnetic ground-state formation by incorporating many-body electron correlations.
DFT+DMFT explains ferromagnetic ground-state formation by incorporating thermal fluctuations.
CoCrFeMnNi is an example of a high-entropy alloy system to which the proposed analysis might be applied.
Standard DFT indicates magnetic ordering in the proposed transition-metal alloy.
Standard DFT underestimates electron-correlation effects in the proposed alloy.
Systematically tuning U in DFT+DMFT captures enhanced many-body interactions.
At low or zero temperature, thermal fluctuations are minimal and many-body interactions dominate the electronic structure.
Local magnetic moments and the local electronic structure can be represented through atom-resolved magnetic quantities.
The d-orbital contributions and local magnetic moments mediate magnetic exchange interactions.
DFT+DMFT provides a more rigorous treatment of local electron-electron correlations than standard DFT.
DFT+DMFT captures fluctuations of local magnetic moments and dynamical correlation effects.
An improved description of double exchange and local-moment formation stabilizes ferromagnetic ordering.
DFT+DMFT will predict a robust ferromagnetic ground state with enhanced and consistent local magnetic moments.
Standard spin-polarized DFT typically fails to capture the many-body correlations responsible for stabilizing the ferromagnetic ground state.
The proposed approach is most effective for materials with significant electron correlation.
The accuracy of DFT+DMFT depends on proper selection of the U parameter.
DFT+DMFT may be less predictive for highly itinerant magnets or systems with weak electron localization.
Quantitative magnetic moments and magnetic-state energy differences depend on the chosen U values and require experimental calibration.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis credits incorporation of thermal fluctuations with explaining the ferromagnetic ground state, whereas the conditions require low or zero temperature so that thermal fluctuations are minimal.
